key_insight: In simulated motivational interviewing sessions, prompting AI therapists for greater empathy, affirmation, and alliance building improved AI-rated treatment integrity.
clinical_relevance: This proof of concept suggests AI simulations could help study psychotherapy processes, but it does not establish benefits for real patients.
method: Preregistered experiment generating 512 therapist–patient simulations with locally deployed Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct models.
Compared high versus low common therapeutic factors across eight vignettes and eight therapist personas.
Used blinded, repeated LLM ratings and mixed-effects analysis, with human coding of a stratified subsample.
evidence_signal: Of 512 simulations, 480 were analyzed; high-factor prompts improved all MITI global ratings (β = 0.54–0.95; all p < 0.001).
watch_item: Both conversations and primary ratings were AI-generated, so findings may reflect model-specific patterns rather than real therapeutic effects.
paper_title: Simulating Psychotherapeutic Sessions with Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Proof-of-Concept Study of In Silico Psychotherapy Research
